subject: Day 71: start a freezer milk stash
bodyText:
Today's focus
With Avi feeding predictably, this is the week to operationalize the return-to-work logistics. Today's lead is building a freezer stash so a daycare or nanny handoff does not start from zero.

Action items
- If Anoushka is returning to work, start a pumping rhythm now: one to two sessions a day, targeting roughly 2 oz of frozen milk per missed feed. Building the stash gradually protects supply better than a last-minute sprint.
- Stage the pumping kit Anoushka will need: an insulated cooler bag, a spare set of pump parts, and a labeling system for dated bottles.
- Confirm the daycare or nanny start date lines up with the return-to-work date, ideally with a one-to-two-week overlap buffer. Childcare.gov: https://www.childcare.gov/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Profuse drooling and hand-sucking. This reflects salivary-gland maturation, not necessarily teething; first teeth typically arrive at six to 10 months.
- [monitor] Persistent head tilt to one side with limited rotation; flag possible torticollis for a physical-therapy referral.
- [call within 24h] Acute new fever onset, or persistent vomiting lasting more than 24 hours.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, an apnea or color-change episode, or seizure-like activity. Call 911 if his lips turn blue!

Enrichment opportunities
- Build the pumping stash as a household project, not an afterthought: a steady one-to-two-session rhythm is what keeps the social handoff to a caregiver smooth when leave ends.
- Play one instrument's recording on repeat for five to 10 minutes during play, such as violin if you are considering Suzuki; pre-Suzuki listening exposure can begin this early with no downside. Suzuki Association: https://suzukiassociation.org/
- Read a board book with a repeated refrain so Avi can start anticipating the pattern; repeated-refrain text drives predictive language processing. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/

Upcoming
- Day 84-91 (~3 months): sleep-consolidation window opens; begin a consistent sleep-wake routine.
- Day 112-126 (4-month visit): RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete

- Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pushes-up-on-elbows/complete

- Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-toy-when-placed/complete

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete
